text.p: The Philippine Senate and House of Representatives decided on Wednesday to end a month-long deadlock over the 1997 national budget, lawmakers said.

Senator Ernesto Herrera, finance committee chairman, said both houses agreed to cut their countrywide development fund (CDF) entitlements, the cause of the impasse. Legislators can use the fund for development works in their constituencies.

The opposition-dominated Senate had feared the administration-backed House would use the fund for early campaigning ahead of the 1998 presidential and congressional elections. The Senate had slashed the 1997 budget by about 82.6 billion pesos to 392.35 billion pesos.
The House had already passed the budget but the Senate's blocking it led to the government passing special appropriation bills to meet expenditures this year.

The Senate had agreed to a 40 percent slash in its current CDF allotment of 18 million pesos for each senator, while the House will have a 10 percent cut in the 12.5 million-peso CDF for each legislator, Herrera said.
Lawmakers also agreed to be transparent as to where the CDF money will be spent, he said.

"The House of Representatives expects to ratify the proposed 1997 national budget tonight or tomorrow (Wednesday or Thursday), thus paving the way for its signing by President (Fidel) Ramos on Friday next week," said House Speaker Jose de Venecia in a statement.
Socio-economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said the delay in the passage of the 1997 budget had affected government projects.
